title: Preliminary object request list — Research Demo 001
note: Research aid generated from simulation contradictions and metadata gaps. Not an automatic ranking algorithm.

candidates.title: Model, Trylon and Perisphere
candidates.whyRequest: Two agents read its futuristic form as technological optimism while others question what physical construction, labor, materiality, and scale disappear from the digital representation.
candidates.generatingContradiction: Futurist liberation/optimism vs Worker/Archivist insistence that liberation is not established by catalog fields.
onsiteQuestions: Examine joins, surface, construction method, rear/underside, material transitions, and any object information unavailable in the public representation of the Trylon and Perisphere model.
Which seams, fasteners, revisions, labels, or backside information on the physical model are absent from the published descriptive fields?

candidates.title: Radio, Sparton, model 558-C
candidates.whyRequest: Propagandist and Futurist treat streamlining as domestication of mass media; Archivist requires advertising files; Worker/Mourner ask what labor and asymmetric listening the object holds.
candidates.generatingContradiction: Persuasion-by-design inference vs source-supported identity-only reading; Counterfeit leisure statistic rejected.
onsiteQuestions: How did designers make a potentially unfamiliar mass-media technology feel desirable, legible, safe, and domestic—and what traces remain on the Sparton radio?
What dial markings, wear, repair history, or manufacturer labels on the physical radio are not captured in the short public description?

candidates.title: Vase with lid, Mappemonde [Globe]
candidates.whyRequest: Museum-published colonial-display framing conflicts with Futurist progress readings; physical decoration and related materials are needed to test the contradiction.
candidates.generatingContradiction: Mourner colonial-display reading vs Futurist/Propagandist progress/allegiance readings.
onsiteQuestions: How do staff and labels currently handle colonial display objects beside utopian fair materials?
What maker marks, lid fit, and decorative zones become legible only in person?

candidates.title: Catalogue, Machine Age Exposition
candidates.whyRequest: Machine ideology document spans aesthetic praise and possible occlusion of labor; handling the volume tests image hierarchy and essay order.
candidates.generatingContradiction: Mechanical beauty as liberation curriculum vs Worker/Mourner occlusion-of-labor readings.
onsiteQuestions: Which plates or captions in the physical catalogue make labor visible, and which aestheticize machinery into pure form?
What annotations, ownership marks, paper quality, or inserted ephemera appear only when the catalogue is handled as a library object?
